system.summary: Graphic-sign simple substitution with a few homophones (a, i/a, w/u, g), words divided, inserted as runs in clear English.
system.sibling_key: none used (cobham1588 session confirmed the same forms from glosses on f. 89, R8493, after this key was built)
system.notes: Key R8497 in the same volume (Bodley 1590) is a different system.

prior_solution.where: DECODE lists the records as partially/non-decrypted; no decipherment on the leaves; CSP Foreign 1588 calendars other Cobham letters but not these

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the seven page images and the key record R8497 from DECODE with the session cookie.
Checked CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, March 1588 sections, for these letters.
Compared the Bodley 1590 key R8497 in the same volume.
Cipher runs beside clear words read as 'commaunded to attend', 'that bearer hath', 'instructions', 'under colour thereof', 'any money', fixing most letters.
Read the runs of ff. 70r-72v word by word from context; long runs on f. 70v and 71v read in sense (preparations, eleven companies of footmen, subject to interception).
The cobham1588 session found the same letter values in the contemporary glosses of f. 89 (R8493).

outcome.notes: Most runs on ff. 70v, 71v, 72r read; about a third of f. 70r, two names on f. 72r and the last line of f. 71r open. f. 11 (R8477) is a different letter and code, not read.
